h1: Forra Dive Resort Pattaya Beach — beachfront bamboo bungalows for budget divers on Koh Lipe
intro: If you come to Koh Lipe mainly to dive and don't need a polished air-con room, Forra Dive Resort on Pattaya Beach is the place a lot of divers pick · It's a cluster of bamboo and wooden bungalows right on the sand at the western end of Pattaya Beach — a quieter corner with fewer longtail boats than the middle, yet still a 7-minute walk to Walking Street · The real draw is the on-site PADI/SSI dive centre, whose instructors get glowing reviews · From around ฿900/night for a bamboo bungalow · score 7.3 — a rustic stay where you need to know exactly what you're getting.

body.html: Forra Dive Resort has a clear identity — it's a dive centre's resort, not a hotel that happens to run dive trips · Almost everything is built from bamboo and wood, set at the western end of Pattaya Beach, a calmer corner of the main beach with fewer longtails pulling in · If you're here to do an Open Water course or dive several days in a row and want a place where you walk from your bungalow to the dive centre and to the sand in a few steps, this is about as on-the-nose as it gets for that kind of use.

Rooms split into two clear groups · The first is roughly 10 bamboo bungalows — fan-cooled, with mosquito nets, the cheapest option, leaning into simple eco living: no air-con, no frills · The second is 9 wooden deluxe bungalows, including beachfront, partial sea-view and two-storey/family units, which are noticeably roomier and more comfortable · The key thing to know before booking: if you expect cold air-con and a spotless bathroom, the bamboo bungalows are not that — they're about sleeping close to nature by the sea on a budget, so match the room to what you actually want.

"Did my dive course here, the instructor was so patient. From the bamboo bungalow to the dive centre is just a few steps — wake up and you're in the water. But the room really is basic, you have to be ready for that."

The heart of the place is the beachfront dive centre · Forra runs standard PADI, SSI and CMAS courses plus liveaboard trips · A large share of reviews single out the instructors as patient, professional and good at putting nervous swimmers at ease — it's what brings people back · Out front there's a wooden clubhouse, a beach bar and a seaside restaurant called Kioskino serving Western and Italian food, a nice spot to sit over the sunset · Being on the western end of Pattaya Beach also makes it a good sunset-watching corner.

The honest part is condition and cleanliness · Because these are bamboo bungalows in a natural setting, some reviews mention insects, mosquitoes and termite marks in certain units, and cleanliness that isn't always consistent · A few basics may need to be brought yourself (soap, in some rooms) · Another recurring point is that the price feels high relative to the room standard, especially compared with similarly priced stays on the island, and the on-site restaurant isn't cheap · This is why Forra suits divers for whom the dive package adds the value more than travellers simply chasing the lowest room rate.

What makes the numbers more interesting is the dive-day deal — in low season the resort offers free bamboo-bungalow nights on days you dive, and in high season a room discount on dive days · If you plan to dive several days in a row, that changes the value equation entirely: pay for the diving and the beachfront bed comes close to free · TripAdvisor rates it 3.9/5, ranked #10 of 64 stays on Koh Lipe, with an overall score around 7.3 on booking platforms — reflecting strong diving and a good beachfront location, with the rooms and cleanliness pulling the score down.

Honestly, Forra Dive Resort isn't for everyone · If you're coming to Koh Lipe to relax in comfort, want cold air-con and a spotless bathroom, and have no interest in diving, other island options serve you better at a similar budget · But if you're a diver, or you want to try a rustic bamboo bungalow right on the sand in a quieter corner of Pattaya Beach, watch the sunset, and wake up straight into the water — and you weight dive-school quality over room polish — this place has a particular charm that's hard to find elsewhere.

Tips drawn from the reviews: if the budget allows, step up from a bamboo bungalow to a wooden deluxe beachfront unit — far more comfortable and better value as an experience · If you're set on diving, sort out a course + dive-day stay package with the resort in advance to get the best deal · Bring your own mosquito repellent and toiletries · And note that in low season (roughly mid-May to mid-October) many Koh Lipe stays close, so check with the resort before planning a trip in that window.

honestSummary: Forra Dive Resort Pattaya Beach suits divers who weight dive-school quality and a beachfront spot over room polish — bamboo and wooden bungalows on the quieter west end of Pattaya Beach, an on-site dive centre, and dive-day deals that improve the value · But accept that the rooms are simple and rustic, the bamboo bungalows are fan-only, there are mosquitoes and insects, cleanliness isn't always consistent, and the price runs high for the room standard.
honestChecks: If you want cold air-con and a spotless bathroom — bamboo bungalows are fan-only and very basic → step up to a wooden deluxe beachfront unit, or look at other island stays in a similar budget.
If you're not here mainly to dive — the real value is the dive centre and the dive-day deals → without diving, the price relative to room condition may be less worth it than other options.

If you're sensitive to mosquitoes and insects — bamboo bungalows in a natural setting attract them → bring repellent, always use the mosquito net provided, and pick a unit recent reviews praise for cleanliness.

faqTitle: FAQ — Forra Dive Resort Pattaya Beach, Koh Lipe

faq.q: Where is Forra Dive Resort Pattaya Beach, and how do you get there?
faq.a: It sits at the western end of Pattaya Beach on Koh Lipe, Satun Province — a quieter corner of the main beach with fewer longtail boats than the middle · To reach Koh Lipe you take a speedboat from Pak Bara or Tammalang pier (Satun), about 1.5 hours · From the Pattaya Beach landing you walk to the resort, and it's about a 7-minute walk to Walking Street.

faq.q: What does Forra Dive Resort cost, and what rooms are there?
faq.a: Prices start around ฿900/night for a fan-cooled bamboo bungalow (with mosquito net) in the normal range · They step up to wooden deluxe bungalows and beachfront wooden bungalows that are roomier and more comfortable · Rates vary by season; high season (Nov–Apr) climbs sharply, so compare platforms and book ahead.

faq.q: Who is Forra Dive Resort best for?
faq.a: Best for divers and travellers who like a rustic, close-to-nature stay · The standout is the beachfront PADI/SSI dive centre with well-reviewed instructors, plus dive-day deals that improve the value · It's not for those who want polished air-con rooms, consistent cleanliness, or a relaxed stay without diving.

faq.q: Do the bamboo bungalows have air-con, and what condition are they in?
faq.a: The bamboo bungalows are fan-cooled with a mosquito net, no air-con, leaning into simple eco living close to nature · Some reviews mention mosquitoes, insects and termite marks in certain units, and cleanliness that isn't always consistent · For more comfort, step up to a wooden deluxe bungalow and bring mosquito repellent.

faq.q: What is diving with Forra like, and are there any deals?
faq.a: Forra is a dive centre running standard PADI, SSI and CMAS courses plus liveaboard trips, with instructors widely praised as patient and professional · There are deals that improve value on dive days — free bamboo-bungalow nights in low season, room discounts in high season — so arrange a package with the resort in advance.

faq.q: When should you visit Koh Lipe, and do stays close in low season?
faq.a: Koh Lipe's high season is November–April: clear water, good weather, rooms fill fast and rates climb, so book months ahead · In low season (roughly mid-May to mid-October) the sea is rougher and many island stays close, so check with the resort before planning a trip then.
